About the role

We're hiring our first Security Operations Lead to build and run the SecOps function at Fireworks AI. This role sits within the Security team and will primarily support Corporate Security and own incident response broadly, while partnering closely with Security Engineering on infrastructure-related incidents — bridging both areas. This is an IC-to-manager role: you’ll start hands-on building and running the function, growing into a people leader as the team scales.

What you'll do

 - Lead the rollout, tuning, and ongoing operation of CrowdStrike across our endpoint and cloud environment and SIEM use cases, partnering with IT and Security Engineering on deployment and coverage

 - Define and operate our detection and response program: build detection content, establish triage and escalation workflows, and continuously measure and improve coverage against frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK

 - Own incident response end-to-end: operationalize our existing SIRP into detailed playbooks, run incidents, lead post-incident reviews, and drive lessons learned into program improvements

 - Partner closely with Infrastructure, Corporate Security, and other cross-functional teams across the organization, engaging as needed to support incidents and shared initiatives

How the role will grow

As the function matures, you'll have the opportunity to:

 - Hire and build the SecOps team, growing from IC to people leader

 - Expand 24x7 coverage and adjacent capabilities like cloud detection engineering, insider threat, or red team / purple team operations

 - Shape the broader security strategy as a senior leader in the function

 - 7+ years in security operations, detection and response, incident response, or a closely related field

 - Hands-on experience with EDR platforms (CrowdStrike strongly preferred; SentinelOne, Defender, or similar also relevant) including detection engineering and tuning

 - Strong detection engineering background: you've written, tested, and maintained detection content at scale and understand the tradeoffs between coverage, fidelity, and analyst load

 - Demonstrated incident response leadership: you've run real incidents from triage through executive communication and post-incident review

 - Strong scripting and automation skills (Python, SOAR platforms) applied to detection, response, and reporting workflows

 - Working knowledge of cloud security operations (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and the unique telemetry, attack patterns, and response considerations of cloud-native environments

 - Experience building or significantly maturing a SecOps function, including tooling selection, process design, and metrics

 - Comfort operating in a build phase: you can write the playbook and run the playbook, and you know when to invest in process versus when to just get things done

Nice to have

 - Experience with Incident.io http://Incident.io, PagerDuty, or comparable incident management tooling

 - Prior experience at an AI, cloud infrastructure, or high-growth SaaS company

 - Certifications such as GCIA, GCIH, GCFA, OSCP, or similar

ABOUT THE ROLE

Compensation touches nearly every decision we make about talent. We’re hiring our first dedicated Compensation Partner — the person responsible for translating our compensation philosophy into practice.

You'll build the connective tissue between what we believe about pay and how pay decisions actually get made across a fast-growing org. That means bringing rigor to how we benchmark, review, and adjust compensation — and building the systems and processes that let that rigor hold as we scale. You'll own it end to end and hands-on: running the market research, designing the review cycle, keeping the data clean, and serving as the person HRBPs and leaders turn to when a pay question needs a real answer. You'll also partner closely with Finance to shape our equity structure through a compensation lens.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Translate our compensation philosophy into clear strategy and practice

 - Take our existing compensation philosophy and turn it into practical guardrails, bands, and decision frameworks that managers and HRBPs can actually use

 - Regularly check that our real-world pay practices stay aligned with our philosophy, flagging and correcting drift as we grow

 - Keep our compensation posture competitive and agile — able to respond to market shifts rather than only revisiting pay once a year

Maintain and evolve our compensation bands

 - Own our job architecture and salary bands, keeping them current as roles, levels, and the market evolve

 - Run ongoing market research and benchmarking (survey data, competitive intelligence) to ensure our bands remain competitive

 - Recommend band adjustments proactively, rather than waiting for a leader or HRBP to flag a problem

Own compensation data, analysis, and systems

 - Maintain accurate compensation data and be the source of truth Finance, People Ops, and HRBPs rely on

 - Own compensation system implementation and administration (e.g., HRIS/Workday compensation modules), keeping the process scalable as headcount grows

 - Turn compensation data into clear analysis and recommendations for leadership — pay equity, competitiveness, spend trends

Build and run our compensation review program

 - Design and own the end-to-end compensation review cycle — timing, guardrails, manager tools, and calibration approach

 - Partner with HRBPs to roll the program out across their orgs, adapting company-level design to what actually works for each function

 - Build the manager-facing tools and guidance that keep pay decisions consistent and defensible across teams

Participate in designing our benefits strategy

 - Own the strategic direction of our benefits program across geographies — what we offer, how it evolves, and how it stays competitive and cost-effective as we scale

 - Partner with People Ops, who continue to own day-to-day benefits administration, to ensure strategy and execution stay connected

 - Evolve the benefits framework as we expand into new locations or hit new headcount milestones

Partner with Finance on equity

 - Bring strong familiarity with equity compensation design (options, RSUs, or similar) to partner closely with Finance in building out a robust equity framework

 - Support equity-related modeling, guidelines, and decision-making as part of the broader compensation strategy

 - Help ensure equity practices stay consistent with our overall compensation philosophy

Be the go-to comp expert for HRBPs and leaders

 - Act as subject matter expert on pay decisions, offer approvals, and job evaluations

 - Educate and enable HRBPs and managers so they can confidently make and explain compensation decisions within our frameworks


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 6+ years of progressive compensation experience, ideally including time maintaining and evolving comp programs (bands, review cycles, market benchmarking) in a fast-growing company

 - Direct experience with equity compensation (options, RSUs, or similar) and comfort partnering with Finance on equity framework design

 - Strong analytical foundation: comfortable with market data, compensation modeling, and translating data into clear recommendations

 - A hands-on, do-er mindset — comfortable owning the process and the details, not just setting direction for others to execute

 - Experience partnering with HRBPs, Finance, and People Ops as equal stakeholders

 - Excellent written communication — able to explain compensation mechanics clearly to audiences ranging from executives to first-time managers

 - Familiarity with relevant compensation systems and survey data sources (e.g., Workday, Radford, Pave, Carta Total Comp)

Nice to have
